widgets_values:
FLARECORE STUDIO

Three benches, one switch. Click a bench
on the Flarecore Studio node:

  Element forge - make new elements
  Flare lab     - design the flare
  Video lab     - track it over footage

The two inactive benches grey out and
are muted, so Queue only runs the one
you are working in.

widgets_values_named.text:
FLARECORE STUDIO

Three benches, one switch. Click a bench
on the Flarecore Studio node:

  Element forge - make new elements
  Flare lab     - design the flare
  Video lab     - track it over footage

The two inactive benches grey out and
are muted, so Queue only runs the one
you are working in.

widgets_values:
VIDEO LAB - one node does the work\n\nLoad Video -> Flare Render -> Combine. Tracking, depth conditioning
and the light source all live inside Flare Render (open the gear).

Pick the light source from the LIGHT SOURCE dropdown at the top of
the panel - each mode shows only its own controls:
  manual      - drag the light on the picker.
  detect      - brightest spot, each frame on its own.
  track       - the same, followed through the clip. This is the one
                for footage. If the flare wanders between nearby
                lights, lower track_max_jump.
  track_dots  - a black plate with white dots: every dot gets its own
                flare, with its own identity across the clip. Raise
                detect_max_lights to the number of dots you expect.
                The threshold is relative to the brightest thing in
                the clip, so a matte that never reaches pure white
                still works. Take flare_pass to composite the result
                over your real footage.
  path        - draw the light's route. Choosing this mode arms the
                picker: click to drop a point, drag to move one,
                shift-click to remove. The light travels the whole
                path across the clip, so put points closer together
                where you want it to slow down.

Depth is optional: wire a raw depth model straight into depth and set
depth_normalize to per_batch. Flare Depth Adapter still exists if you
want level remapping or per-frame modes.

The flare animates itself as the light moves: rows with a RED EDGE in
the editor carry a trigger rule, and the lens row has flicker and
edge fade. Both outputs: composite, and the flare over black.

widgets_values:
FLARE LAB

1. Drag the orange LIGHT point and the cyan FLARE ANCHOR directly on
   the picker at the top of Flare Render. Ghost spacing follows the
   distance between the two points.
2. Build the flare in the editor below it: + add, then the
   pos / size / opac sliders. The chevron on a row opens the full
   parameter set (colour, dispersion, count chains, triggers...).
   Click an element's NAME to swap it for one of your own from the
   family gallery.
3. presets loads shipped looks; save... writes your own next to them.
   The gear reveals the node's inputs; everything else stays hidden.
4. flare_pass is the flare over black for external compositing.

Depth occlusion lives in the VIDEO bench, where the footage is -
wire any depth map into Flare Render's depth input to use it here.

The panels hide below ~50% zoom - a ComfyUI DOM widget rule.

widgets_values:
ELEMENT FORGE (Krea2)

1. On the element prompt panel: pick a category, then an element.
   Its prompt appears below, ready to edit - what you see is exactly
   what is queued. The extra style line is appended only while its
   toggle is on.
2. Queue: Krea2 generates, Flare Texture Prepare conditions it, and
   Flare Element Save files it under elements/<category>/<name>.png.
   For lens plates (dirt, droplets) set frame = wide_16_9 on Prepare.
3. Use it: in the Flare Lab editor, click any element's NAME to pick
   your new file from its family gallery.
4. Bump the sampler seed for variations; luminance mode makes
   tintable neutral elements, rgb keeps the generated colour.
